inside_destinations.note: 32 spots of six proposed destinations; a further five kept candidates (Broome, Derby, Kununurra, Wyndham, Purnululu National Park) are the destinations themselves

stronger_left_out.name: Canning Stock Route
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): A route, not a place you stop at for half an hour; Wikivoyage calls it beyond its scope; most of its length and its southern trailhead (Wiluna) lie outside the Kimberley (probably wa-golden-outback / Pilbara), so the proposer must decide one region and pin it at the midpoint; permits needed.

stronger_left_out.name: Gwion Gwion Rock Paintings
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Not one place: an art style found at hundreds of remote sites, mostly reached on guided tours or flights (an operator), and the candidate has no coordinates; better listed as a named accessible site (e.g. on the Mitchell Falls walk or near Kalumburu) if a source names one, otherwise mentioned in a destination description.

stronger_left_out.name: Bungle Bungle Range
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 3 duplicate of Purnululu National Park: the range is the park's headline landform and the park is named for the place (COVERAGE: a park destination is named as the park); kept as one under Purnululu National Park.

stronger_left_out.name: Buccaneer Archipelago
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Visitors go for Horizontal Falls, a candidate of its own inside the archipelago; the archipelago as a whole is an area seen only from boats and planes, so it risks being a near-duplicate wrapper of Horizontal Falls.

stronger_left_out.name: Kalumburu
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Neither source names something to see in the community itself, only the two permits needed to enter; access is at the Traditional Owners' discretion and may be closed. The candidate note is wrong: Mitchell Falls is reached from a turn-off on Kalumburu Road, not from Kalumburu.

stronger_left_out.name: Gibb River Road
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): A road is the way you get there, and its places (Windjana, Tunnel Creek, Bell, Galvans, Manning, Emma gorges, El Questro) are spots of their own (A spot is a place); the owner should decide whether a 647 km 4WD route is a spot, pinned at its midpoint.

stronger_left_out.name: Warmun
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Only one-line mentions, no own guide section, and an Aboriginal community where the visitor draw is the art centre rather than the town: the Warmun Art Centre may be the right spot, or it is a gateway village whose draw is the journey beyond (Pipiriki benchmark -> review).

stronger_left_out.name: James Price Point
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Re-looked for a counted source and found none: only science news on the Walmadany dinosaur tracks and a Q&A travel blog that says there are no tourist facilities; the tracks are intertidal and visible only at low tide (rule 1 fails).

stronger_left_out.name: Cape Leveque
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Kooljaman, the resort that held the visitor access, closed indefinitely on 1 Nov 2021 and no reopening was found; an operator says Cape Leveque point is closed indefinitely and access is limited (rule 2: open to the public is unconfirmed).

stronger_left_out.name: Roebuck Bay
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: An area, not a stop: visitors reach the bay at Broome Bird Observatory and Town Beach, both candidates of their own, so the bay is a near-duplicate of them (rule 3). Wikivoyage Broome names it only in passing.

stronger_left_out.name: Beagle Bay
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Duplicate of Sacred Heart Church, Beagle Bay: the only thing any visitor source names here is the church (Wikivoyage Kimberley), so the community is a wrapper around its own attraction (COVERAGE: a town is a spot only when the town itself is a draw).

stronger_left_out.name: One Arm Point
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Several operators report the hatchery closed for repairs after cyclone damage; a community permit is needed; without the hatchery the draw is the views and crafts only.

stronger_left_out.name: Camballin
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 2: a town with nothing a source names to see; Wikivoyage gives one line ('has fishing on the Fitzroy River') and lists it only as a place the highway passes; no accommodation per source. (Audit disagreed: script keep, auditor review; verdicts.json records reject, so it is not placed; the owner may treat it as review.)

stronger_left_out.name: Pioneer Cemetery, Wyndham
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 3: minor historic cemetery; Wikivoyage gives it one line (12 meatworks graves) and no other visitor source singles it out; the 1,592 views are borrowed from an unrelated title.

stronger_left_out.name: Home Valley Station
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): It is a station resort (accommodation business); the gorges and Cockburn Range views it offers are the places, and none is named here as a spot.

stronger_left_out.name: Drysdale River National Park
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 2: DBCA page (fetched) says there is no vehicle access and no infrastructure, entry by permit only (not issued Jan-May), best seen from a scenic flight; a rarely visited wilderness that a visitor cannot simply go to (COVERAGE: rarely visited places fail).

stronger_left_out.name: Lombadina
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Only one counted source and that one not readable now; the community's own site is an operator page; a visit is on community terms with seasonal weekend closures, and the beach and church are modest.

stronger_left_out.name: Mount Elizabeth Station
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Brief: accommodation and stations are rejected as businesses; the gorges are the places and should be the spots if sources name them. Keep only if the station itself is treated as a destination base.

stronger_left_out.name: Piccaninny Crater
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 2: Wikivoyage Purnululu says it 'can really only be seen from the air'; eroded beyond recognition on the ground, with no visitor access or trail, so a visitor cannot go and see it.

stronger_left_out.name: MV Koolama
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Visible only at low tide and only from the wharf; a ten-minute look with a single source.

stronger_left_out.name: Cape Londonderry
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Re-looked for a counted source and found none: it appears only in a cruise operator's helicopter-flight brochure; no road access and nothing a visitor can do there (rules 1 and 2).

stronger_left_out.name: Mornington Wilderness Camp
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Closed: Wikivoyage Gibb River Road says 'Mornington Camp has closed down' (rule 2), and it is an operator's camp rather than a place.

stronger_left_out.name: Kimberley Marine Park
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 2 and 3: a marine-park administrative zone along the whole coast, not a place a visitor goes to; its draws (Horizontal Falls, Montgomery Reef, King George Falls) are judged on their own.

stronger_left_out.name: Bunuba National Park
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 1: Wikipedia only; no DBCA visitor page found (404) and no tourism listing names it; its visitor sights are listed under their own names.

stronger_left_out.name: Lawley River National Park
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 1: Wikipedia only; no DBCA visitor page (404) or tourism source; no visitor access described.

stronger_left_out.name: Niiwalarra Islands National Park
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 1: Wikipedia only; no DBCA visitor page (404) or tourism listing; offshore islands with no visitor access described.

stronger_left_out.name: Warlibirri National Park
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 1: Wikipedia only; no DBCA visitor page (Explore Parks 404) or tourism source names it as somewhere to go.

stronger_left_out.name: Staircase to the Moon
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Duplicate of Town Beach, Broome: a seasonal phenomenon whose place is Town Beach (Wikivoyage Broome: 'the favourite viewing spot is Town Beach'); keep it as one by putting the phenomenon and its dry-season full-moon dates in Town Beach's bio (brief: a seasonal phenomenon is kept as its place).

stronger_left_out.name: Imintji
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: A service stop (campground and community store) rather than a draw: Wikivoyage Gibb River Road lists an art centre, camping and store; Visit Broome says the store is not open in 2026, so no fuel. Fails rule 2 (a business/services stop) and rule 3 (its visitors are there for Bell Gorge).

stronger_left_out.name: Reddell Beach
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): One passing sentence and nothing to do beyond a quiet beach; close to Gantheaume Point, so it may be a near-duplicate of that stop.

stronger_left_out.name: Kabbarli Lookout
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): One source, which also calls the approach grubby through the port industrial area; a short look, similar red rocks to Gantheaume Point nearby.

stronger_left_out.name: Pearl Luggers
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): It is Willie Creek's pearl showroom: a shop with an attached tour (brief: shops and operators are rejected); one counted source.

stronger_left_out.name: Short Street Gallery
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: A commercial gallery selling art (Wikivoyage Broome: 'for sale'), i.e. a shop (rule 2).

stronger_left_out.name: Broome Fruit Bat Roost
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): One sentence in one source, a dusk-only spectacle with no defined site, and a short look; may be too minor.

stronger_left_out.name: SSJG Heritage Centre
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Opens only weekday mornings Feb-Nov, by donation, a small single-room exhibit; one source.

stronger_left_out.name: Shinju Matsuri
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: A festival held the last two weeks of August (rule 4).

stronger_left_out.name: Broome Turf Club
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: A racecourse with races only May-August (rule 4: a recurring event venue, not a place to visit when you arrive).

stronger_left_out.name: Broome Golf Club
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 2/Leave out: a sports club; Wikivoyage mentions it only in passing, noting most visitors come just for a meal at the clubhouse, i.e. a restaurant.

stronger_left_out.name: Frosty's Pool
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): One sentence in one source; a ten-minute look; probably only worth it alongside the Boab Prison Tree.

stronger_left_out.name: Norval Gallery
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Temporarily closed per Wikivoyage Derby, and a commercial gallery selling art (rule 2).

stronger_left_out.name: One Mile Dinner Camp
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: A picnic spot at the end of the golf course, a local reserve used at sundown (Leave out: local parks and reserves; rule 3, minor historic site).

stronger_left_out.name: Derby Speedway
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: A motorsport venue with races May-October (rule 4: recurring events).

stronger_left_out.name: Mud Crab Races, Derby
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: An event held two or three times a year (rule 4).

stronger_left_out.name: Derby Sportsmen's Club
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: A golf club, a local sports amenity (rule 2).

stronger_left_out.name: Derby Memorial Swimming Pool
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: A local public pool, an amenity rather than a visitor draw (rule 2; Leave out).

stronger_left_out.name: Adcock Gorge
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): One passing line; no second counted source found (Visit Broome and DBCA do not list it); a lesser gorge beside better-known ones.

stronger_left_out.name: Wunnamurra Gorge
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): A bare mention with no description; on a private cattle station reached through it; a marginal place needs two sources.

stronger_left_out.name: Warla Gorge
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): A bare mention with no description; on a private cattle station; a marginal place needs two sources.

stronger_left_out.name: Queen Victoria's Head
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): One line in one source; a look from the road, not a half-hour stop.

stronger_left_out.name: Mitchell Plateau
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 3: duplicate of Mitchell River National Park / Mitchell Falls. The plateau is the park's area; Wikivoyage only names it as the destination of Kalumburu Road, and sources name the falls and park as the place visitors go.

stronger_left_out.name: The Domes
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): For keep: DBCA lists the Domes Walk as its own trail and it is where visitors see the iconic beehives up close; if the range itself is listed as the park or a broad area, this walk may deserve its own spot.

stronger_left_out.name: The Window
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Rule 3: it is a point along the Piccaninny Creek bed route (the same walk as Piccaninny Creek Lookout and Whip Snake Gorge); DBCA does not give it its own heading. Likely better folded into one Piccaninny Gorge/Creek spot.

stronger_left_out.name: Whip Snake Gorge
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 3: part of a larger route: a side canyon reached by continuing past The Window, a 10 km return extension of the Piccaninny Creek walk; one Wikivoyage line, no separate DBCA entry.

stronger_left_out.name: Piccaninny Creek Lookout
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Rule 3: it branches off the Cathedral Gorge trail and shares the Piccaninny car park with The Domes, Cathedral Gorge and The Window; may be best as one Piccaninny Creek spot rather than a separate lookout.

stronger_left_out.name: Osmand Lookout
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 3: a minor lookout on the Bloodwoods/Escarpment trail beside Echidna Chasm; Wikivoyage gives one line and DBCA only names it as a destination from the Echidna car park, not a draw in itself.

stronger_left_out.name: Diversion Dam
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Rule 3: it is the downstream end of Lake Kununurra and carries the highway; a picnic/fishing pull-out more for locals than visitors; Australia's North West does not single it out.

stronger_left_out.name: Elephant Rock
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Mostly seen from Lily Creek Lagoon or the highway; Wikivoyage says the climb is rough, unmarked and underwhelming, so it may be a view rather than a place to go (near-duplicate of Lily Creek Lagoon).

stronger_left_out.name: Celebrity Tree Park
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Wikivoyage itself says several trees have died and plaques have dropped off, so there is little to see; arguably an ordinary town park (negative benchmark) and the venue of the Ord Valley Muster.

stronger_left_out.name: Lily Creek Lagoon
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Rule 3: a side-arm of Lake Kununurra, so a near-duplicate if Lake Kununurra is kept; a short waterside stop in town.

stronger_left_out.name: Kununurra Museum
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Small volunteer museum with weekday-afternoon hours and no second source; a 'only if you're nearby anyway' stop.

stronger_left_out.name: Lake Kununurra Golf Club
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 2/Leave out: a sports club; Wikivoyage lists it as a golf course, not an attraction a traveller goes out of their way for.

stronger_left_out.name: Kununurra Leisure Centre
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 2: a local gym and public pool (amenity), not a visitor attraction.

stronger_left_out.name: Ord Valley Muster
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 4: a week-long annual festival in May, not a permanent place; belongs in Kununurra's best-time text.

stronger_left_out.name: Kununurra Agricultural Show
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 4: an event (two days in mid July per Wikivoyage's Events section), not a permanent place.

stronger_left_out.name: Kununurra Race Club
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 4: a venue that only matters on race and rodeo days in the dry season; otherwise nothing to see.

stronger_left_out.name: Afghan Cemetery, Wyndham
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Rule 3: a small historic cemetery and a short look; only one counted source; may be a minor memorial.

stronger_left_out.name: Wyndham Museum
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Volunteer-run with erratic hours, open Apr-Oct 10-2 only; a short visit; may be closed when a visitor arrives (rule 2/4 risk).

stronger_left_out.name: Fisherman's Jetty, Wyndham
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 3: a working fishing jetty given one line in Wikivoyage as a place to spot saltwater crocodiles; no second source and not a distinct draw.

stronger_left_out.name: Three Mile Valley
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): No distance, trail or managing agency named; possibly a local walk only. Needs a second source before it goes in.

stronger_left_out.name: Prison Boab Memorial Swimming Pool
stronger_left_out.reason: What qualifies: Rule 2: a town swimming pool (local amenity), not a visitor attraction.

stronger_left_out.name: Chinatown
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Rule 2: Wikivoyage describes it as mainly shops and cafes ('don't expect gongs'); without a second source naming something to see (heritage buildings, Sun Pictures, pearl showrooms) it is a shopping strip. Name 'Chinatown' needs a wiki disambiguator.

stronger_left_out.name: Chamberlain Gorge
stronger_left_out.reason: Review (owner decides): Rule 3 and 2: inside El Questro Wilderness Park and seen only on the operator's boat cruise (May-Sep), so it may be part of an El Questro spot rather than distinct.

stronger_left_out_note: Every left-out candidate scoring above the lowest kept (0 views, 0 counted sources) is listed; each has the judge's What-qualifies reason (rejects) or the skeptic's objection (reviews). The highest-scored ones: Canning Stock Route (review; wa-golden-outback places it), Gwion Gwion Rock Paintings (review: an art style at hundreds of sites, not one place), Bungle Bungle Range (merged into the Purnululu destination itself), Buccaneer Archipelago (review: fold into Horizontal Falls), Kalumburu (review: permits, nothing named to see), Gibb River Road (review as a spot; proposed as a destination). No strong outsider is left out without a concrete reason.

strongest_outsiders.name: Buccaneer Archipelago
strongest_outsiders.reason: Review: Visitors go for Horizontal Falls, a candidate of its own inside the archipelago; the archipelago as a whole is an area seen only from boats and planes, so it risks being a near-duplicate wrapper of Horizontal Falls.

strongest_outsiders.name: Kalumburu
strongest_outsiders.reason: Review: Neither source names something to see in the community itself, only the two permits needed to enter; access is at the Traditional Owners' discretion and may be closed. The candidate note is wrong: Mitchell Falls is reached from a turn-off on Kalumburu Road, not from Kalumburu.

strongest_outsiders.name: Warmun
strongest_outsiders.reason: Review: Only one-line mentions, no own guide section, and an Aboriginal community where the visitor draw is the art centre rather than the town: the Warmun Art Centre may be the right spot, or it is a gateway village whose draw is the journey beyond (Pipiriki benchmark -> review).

strongest_outsiders.name: James Price Point
strongest_outsiders.reason: What qualifies: Re-looked for a counted source and found none: only science news on the Walmadany dinosaur tracks and a Q&A travel blog that says there are no tourist facilities; the tracks are intertidal and visible only at low tide (rule 1 fails).

strongest_outsiders.name: Cape Leveque
strongest_outsiders.reason: Review: Kooljaman, the resort that held the visitor access, closed indefinitely on 1 Nov 2021 and no reopening was found; an operator says Cape Leveque point is closed indefinitely and access is limited (rule 2: open to the public is unconfirmed).

strongest_outsiders.name: Beagle Bay
strongest_outsiders.reason: What qualifies: Duplicate of Sacred Heart Church, Beagle Bay: the only thing any visitor source names here is the church (Wikivoyage Kimberley), so the community is a wrapper around its own attraction (COVERAGE: a town is a spot only when the town itself is a draw).

strongest_outsiders.name: One Arm Point
strongest_outsiders.reason: Review: Several operators report the hatchery closed for repairs after cyclone damage; a community permit is needed; without the hatchery the draw is the views and crafts only.

benchmark.note: The NZ benchmark list (COVERAGE step 6) has no Kimberley places; these are its Kimberley analogues.
benchmark.gateway_village_to_review: Warmun (Purnululu gateway community) sent to review, as Pipiriki would be: pass
benchmark.long_feature_at_its_access: Eighty Mile Beach placed standalone at its main access point (the caravan park), not under a neighbour: pass
benchmark.place_not_vehicle: Horizontal Falls, Montgomery Reef, King George Falls, Prince Regent NP, Lake Argyle and Chamberlain Gorge are the places; no seaplane, cruise or boat tour is a spot: pass
benchmark.phenomenon_not_spot: Staircase to the Moon merged into Town Beach: pass
benchmark.events_rejected: Shinju Matsuri, Ord Valley Muster, Kununurra Agricultural Show, Mud Crab Races, Broome Turf Club, speedway rejected (rule 4): pass
benchmark.amenities_rejected: golf clubs, public pools, leisure centre rejected (rule 2): pass
benchmark.town_wrapper: Beagle Bay rejected as a wrapper for Sacred Heart Church; Broome, Derby, Kununurra and Wyndham are destinations, not spots beside their attractions: pass
benchmark.park_and_feature: Wolfe Creek Crater, Windjana Gorge, Tunnel Creek, Danggu Geikie Gorge kept once each (park and feature one place): pass

lowest_kept_note: Zebedee Springs and China Wall carry 0 counted sources in verdicts.json, though the judge's re-look found Tourism WA attraction pages for both (and Australia's North West for China Wall).
